name_note: GTDB R232 names this species Bifidobacterium vaginale, while the genomes it contains are labelled Gardnerella vaginalis in NCBI, which is the name used in the literature.

sentences.text: The species known in the literature as Gardnerella vaginalis is a bacterium of the human vagina that is associated with bacterial vaginosis.
A study reported it as the predominant species found in most cases of bacterial vaginosis, and noted that asymptomatic women are sometimes colonised with low numbers.
It forms dense adherent biofilms on the vaginal mucosa, which were seen to return once oral metronidazole treatment stopped.
It secretes vaginolysin, a cholesterol-dependent cytolysin that lyses target cells in a species-specific way through the human complement regulatory molecule CD59.
A published conceptual model proposes that bacterial vaginosis begins with sexual transmission of this organism, and the condition has been associated with preterm birth.
